stories.title: 3D Cell Painting reveals drug-response differences obscured in 2D cultures
stories.takeaway: A scalable imaging workflow profiles individual cells within intact spheroids and distinguishes drug effects that are difficult to separate in monolayers.
stories.what_happened: In Nature Communications (October 21), researchers combined tissue clearing, automated focusing and spinning-disk confocal microscopy in 384-well plates. Profiling 52 drugs, they distinguished 5-fluorouracil from olaparib responses in spheroids, with supporting cell-cycle and DNA-damage assays.
stories.why_it_matters: Adds a reproducible, human-relevant phenotypic screening method for advanced 3D tissue models.
stories.caveat: Spheroid imaging and selected drug assays do not establish clinical predictive validity across tissues.

stories.title: Synthetic recordanelles archive transient transcriptomic signals in human cells
stories.takeaway: Genetically encoded RNA-storing compartments preserve cellular transcriptional history for later single-cell analysis.
stories.what_happened: A Nature Biotechnology study (October 21) reports mitochondria-anchored synthetic condensates that recruit and protect endogenous mRNAs for days, capturing transient inducible and interferon responses.
stories.why_it_matters: Offers a potentially useful way to investigate dynamic cell-state responses beyond a conventional single-timepoint RNA-seq snapshot.
stories.caveat: This is a proof-of-concept engineering platform; performance across primary cells and complex tissues requires further validation.

stories.title: Review evaluates microphysiological models of human gastrointestinal disease
stories.takeaway: A new review synthesizes how organoids and organ-on-chip systems model inflammatory, infectious and neoplastic GI disorders.
stories.what_happened: Published online October 5 and included in the October issue of Nature Biomedical Engineering, the review by Peñarete-Acosta and colleagues surveys advances in human-relevant GI models, host microenvironments and translational barriers.
stories.why_it_matters: Provides a public framework for assessing physiological fidelity, scalability and complementary roles of engineered intestinal models.
stories.caveat: This is a review, not newly reported experimental efficacy; the online publication predates today's briefing.

stories.title: New editorial calls for more physiologically faithful human tissue models
stories.takeaway: Nature Biomedical Engineering emphasizes combining complementary experimental systems and improving tissue-specific context.
stories.what_happened: An October 15 editorial surveys organoids, organ chips and microphysiological models, highlighting the importance of mechanical, stromal, immune and barrier features while acknowledging that no single model captures whole-organism physiology.
stories.why_it_matters: A timely field-level perspective on validation and translational expectations for new approach methodologies.
stories.caveat: Editorial perspective rather than original data; published one week before this briefing.

stories.title: New organ-on-chip microscopy workflow integrates intact-chip imaging and ultrastructure
stories.takeaway: A recently accepted methods paper proposes multiscale analysis of organ-on-chip tissue architecture.
stories.what_happened: Frontiers in Bioengineering and Biotechnology lists an October 18 acceptance for a methods article by Gierke and colleagues integrating intact-chip imaging, histopathology and electron microscopy.
stories.why_it_matters: Connects device-scale readouts with tissue morphology and ultrastructure, potentially strengthening characterization of engineered models.
stories.caveat: Accepted listing only; full peer-reviewed article details and final publication are not yet available from the cited listing.
